items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Sonny Greer, who was not a great cymbaler -- but what he did to that band was what I tried to do to push a band, to get underneath it.

ctx.x: Of playing behind the piano or something like -- the piano, mostly, he used to play behind. Outside of the open cymbals, but he used to play with one stick on the side of the high hat, and of course he's the greatest artist in the world -- and the other hand, and I developed a little thing out of that, which you've heard me on any of the records with the small bands that I play, and that got under my skin from Jo Jones. And I could develop this with the

great respect I had -- I couldn't possibly have liked Duke Ellington. Well, just love him, my dear, dear friend -- Sonny Greer, who was not a great cymbaler -- but what he did to that band was what I tried to do to push a band, to get underneath it.
Well, you certainly have done that down through the years.
